properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 27 at 4:08PM AST until October 27 at 5:15PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Guayanilla County in Puerto Rico...
Penuelas County in Puerto Rico...
Ponce County in Puerto Rico...

* WHEN...Until 515 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 408 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
properties.area: Guayanilla, PR; Penuelas, PR; Ponce, PR

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued October 27 at 3:44PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...
Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...
Coastal Waters of Northwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

* At 344 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated strong showers and
thunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. These
strong showers and thunderstorms were moving offshore from
northwestern PR towards the nearshore waters and the western
offshore Atlantic waters. They were moving northwest at 15 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from
10 NM to 19.5N, Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM
and Coastal Waters of Northwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM.
properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until these showers and t-storms pass.

These thunderstorms will likely produce winds to around 30 knots, and
could pose a serious hazard for boaters. Boaters should consider
heading for shore before the storm arrives.
properties.area: Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico AND USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N; Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM; Coastal Waters OF Northwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 1:19PM MDT until October 27 at 3:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding continues, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County, West Central Costilla County,
Southeastern Rio Grande County, and Southwestern Alamosa County...

* WHEN...Until 345 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring, especially in areas along
and near the Conejos River and the Rio Grande. Widespread
inundation of agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying
areas persists. Areas of standing or slow moving water will
continue over many roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 114 PM MDT, Flooding was still occurring in the warning area,
especially in low-lying areas.
- Low lying areas in Conejos, Costilla, Rio Grande and Alamosa
counties are impacted, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
properties.area: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO; Rio Grande, CO

properties.description:

Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the
coastal waters of Saint Croix...
Coastal Waters of Southern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

isolated thunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30
knots. These showers were located just offshore of Penuelas and
Guayanilla along a southeastern line through offshore Caribbean
waters, moving northwest at 10 knots.

These showers will also move inland along the coast.
properties.instruction:

waves, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek safe harbor

could pose a serious hazard for boaters. Boaters should consider

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 11:53AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed to Minor severity and increased in
duration for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday was 6.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.9 feet
this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.9
feet on 06/13/1991.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Wednesday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 11:47AM MDT until October 29 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At the initial flood stage of 19.5 feet, the water level
in the Lower Rio Puerco will begin to threaten several homes and
structures in the village of San Francisco between Interstate 25
and the Rio Grande. Further rises in water levels would begin to
flood the village of San Francisco.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday was 24.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.4 feet
tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.5
feet on 08/10/2006 and a similar crest on 10/03 of this current
month.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 9:07AM MDT until October 29 at 4:17AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

Purgatoire River Near Las Animas affecting Bent County.

For the Purgatoire River...including Las Animas...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Purgatoire River near Las Animas.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Minor Flood. Minor agricultural flooding
occurs into low lying areas along the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM MDT Tuesday the stage was 8.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon
to 10.2 feet tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood
stage tomorrow afternoon to 3.0 feet Saturday evening. It will
rise to 3.1 feet early Sunday morning. It will then fall again
and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 10.2
feet on 05/31/1995.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM MDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 10:04AM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor and Deland affecting Lake and Volusia
Counties.

.Persistent and gusty northeast winds are slowing river flow. The
river at Astor continues in Moderate flood while the river at Deland
is forecast to reach Minor Flood Stage this afternoon or tonight.
Water levels at both sites are forecast to begin a slow decline late
this week and weekend.

For the St. Johns River at Astor...Moderate flooding is forecast.
For the St. Johns River near Deland...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 3.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 10:04AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor and Deland affecting Lake and Volusia
Counties.

.Persistent and gusty northeast winds are slowing river flow. The
river at Astor continues in Moderate flood while the river at Deland
is forecast to reach Minor Flood Stage this afternoon or tonight.
Water levels at both sites are forecast to begin a slow decline late
this week and weekend.

For the St. Johns River at Astor...Moderate flooding is forecast.
For the St. Johns River near Deland...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Tuesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 26 at 9:20PM CDT until October 27 at 5:00PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande below Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near Presidio, Texas
affecting Presidio County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande above Rio Conchos near
Presidio,  Texas, Test Forecast Point A, Rio Grande at Presidio
Vehicle Bridge, Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near Presidio,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Johnson Ranch near
Castolon,  Texas, Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,  BBNP,  Texas,
Rio Grande near Dryden,  Texas, Terlingua Creek near Terlingua,
Texas...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande below Rio Grande below Rio Conchos near
Presidio, Texas.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, minor flooding continues along the river.
Irrigation pumps may need to be removed.  No threats to residences
or other structures are known to occur. At 9.0 feet, the river
reaches minor flood stage, and low lying areas begin to flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM CDT Monday the stage was 9.6 feet (2.9 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet (2.4 meters).
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:15 PM CDT Monday was 9.7 feet (3.0 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.7 feet
(3.0 meters) late this evening. It will then fall below flood
stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet (2.7 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.7
feet (3.0 meters) on 07/23/2017.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
